summary: Defines the Two Rate Three Color Marker, a meter for Diffserv traffic conditioners. It checks a packet stream against two separate rates and marks packets green, yellow or red depending on which limits they stay within. It is a companion to the single rate version in RFC 2697. This is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2698 describes a meter that labels every Internet packet green, yellow or red, using two speed limits instead of one. A network uses the label to decide which packets to keep and which to drop when traffic is heavy.

how does the trtcm color packets
subtitle: A meter that colors each packet green, yellow or red against a peak rate and a committed rate.

tldr.problem: A Diffserv traffic conditioner sometimes has to enforce a peak rate separately from a committed rate, for example when policing a service at ingress.
tldr.mechanism: Two token buckets, P and C, fill at the rates PIR and CIR up to PBS and CBS, and each packet is marked red if it exceeds the peak rate, otherwise yellow or green depending on whether it exceeds the committed rate.
tldr.outcome: The memo is Informational and specifies no Internet standard. A service may discard red packets, forward yellow packets as best effort, and forward green packets with a low drop probability.

facts.label: Rate unit
facts.value: Bytes of IP packets per second

facts.label: Burst sizes
facts.value: PBS and CBS, both greater than 0

facts.label: Rate rule
facts.value: PIR must be equal to or greater than CIR

today: RFC 2698 is an Informational memo: it does not specify an Internet standard of any kind, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A Meter and a Marker
sections.content:
The Two Rate Three Color Marker (trTCM) is a component of a Diffserv traffic conditioner (RFC 2475, RFC 2474). It meters an IP packet stream and marks its packets green, yellow or red. A packet is marked red if it exceeds the Peak Information Rate (PIR). Otherwise it is marked yellow or green depending on whether it exceeds the Committed Information Rate (CIR).

The Meter meters each packet and passes the packet and the metering result to the Marker, which colors the packet; the color is coded in the DS field of the packet. The Meter operates in one of two modes. In Color-Blind mode it assumes the packet stream is uncolored. In Color-Aware mode it assumes a preceding entity has pre-colored each packet; how that pre-coloring works is specific to the DS domain and outside the scope of the document. A companion, RFC 2697, describes a single rate three color marker.
sections.plainLanguage: One part measures how fast packets arrive, and a second part stamps a color on each one. Two modes let the meter ignore earlier colors or respect them.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.content:
The trTCM is configured by setting its mode and by assigning values to four traffic parameters: a Peak Information Rate (PIR) and its associated Peak Burst Size (PBS), and a Committed Information Rate (CIR) and its associated Committed Burst Size (CBS).

The PIR and CIR are measured in bytes of IP packets per second, which includes the IP header but not link specific headers, and the PIR must be equal to or greater than the CIR. The PBS and the CBS are measured in bytes and both must be configured to be greater than 0. The RFC recommends that they be equal to or greater than the size of the largest possible IP packet in the stream.
sections.plainLanguage: You set two speeds, each with its own burst allowance. The peak speed can never be set below the committed speed, and each burst allowance must be at least one byte.

sections.title: How Metering Works
sections.content:
The behavior of the Meter is specified by its mode and two token buckets, P and C, with rates PIR and CIR. The maximum size of bucket P is PBS and of bucket C is CBS. Both buckets start full: at time 0 the token counts are Tp(0) = PBS and Tc(0) = CBS. Thereafter Tp is incremented one PIR times per second up to PBS, and Tc one CIR times per second up to CBS.

When a packet of size B bytes arrives at time t in Color-Blind mode: if Tp(t)-B < 0 the packet is red; else if Tc(t)-B < 0 the packet is yellow and Tp is decremented by B; else the packet is green and both Tp and Tc are decremented by B. In Color-Aware mode a packet precolored red is red, and a packet precolored yellow is at best yellow, with the same checks applied. The RFC notes that the actual implementation of a Meter does not need to follow this model literally.
sections.plainLanguage: Each packet pays tokens from two buckets. If the peak bucket cannot cover it the packet is red; if only the committed bucket cannot, it is yellow; otherwise it is green.

sections.title: Marking and Service Example
sections.content:
The Marker reflects the metering result by setting the DS field of the packet to a particular codepoint. In case of the AF PHB (RFC 2597), the color can be coded as the drop precedence of the packet.

The trTCM can mark a packet stream in a service that gives different, decreasing levels of assurance to green, yellow and red packets. For example, a service may discard all red packets because they exceeded the peak rate, forward yellow packets as best effort, and forward green packets with a low drop probability. The RFC states that the trTCM has no known security concerns.
sections.plainLanguage: The color tells the network how much to protect the packet. Red packets may be thrown away, yellow packets get normal treatment, and green packets are most likely to be kept.

items.label: Tp(t)-B < 0
items.desc: The packet exceeds the peak rate.

items.label: Tc(t)-B < 0
items.desc: Within the peak rate but over the committed rate; Tp is decremented by B.

items.label: Otherwise
items.desc: Both Tp and Tc are decremented by B.
